comments.value:
I'd like to see some addition warnings/auto-fixes for these differences between WD On and Off since they can make what looks like a simple conversion from On to Off much more annoying without prior knowledge of them:
• When a WD Off state has no animation.
Such states tend to break things. I'm not actually sure what the intended or resulting behaviour is of a WD Off state with no animation, it almost seems to not stop the animation from the previous state when transitioned to.
I always use an 'empty' animation (2 keyframes that animate a shape key of a mesh that doesn't exist) to avoid the issues of WD Off states without animations.
• When non-humanoid Gesture Playable Layer animations are used and there is a WD Off state in a layer in FX that doesn't have an Avatar Mask that prevents the transforms that are animated in the Gesture Playable Layer.
If you're animating transforms in the Gesture Playable Layer, any layer in FX that has WD Off states (with an animation) will prevent the animations of transforms in the Gesture Playable Layer from working, unless the layer in FX also has an Avatar Mask that prevents the transforms (used by the Gesture Playable Layer) from being used.
--
Hai has consolidated a ton of highly useful information on using WD Off and its quirks: https://hai-vr.github.io/combo-gesture-expressions-av3/writedefaults.html

It should be either ON in all controllers, or OFF in all Controllers, you should not Mix them, else it'll break avatar animations.
Mine have them On and seem to not have issues with avatar hider or anything else.

details:
With the latest dev blog, it’s clear that avatar animators with write defaults on will break even more in future updates. However, write defaults on is the Unity default; not only would you not know that it’s discouraged unless you go digging through the documentation, but even if you intend for it to be off it’s very easy to accidentally leave it enabled. The sdk should have guardrails to help protect against this, e.g.:
* alter the editor default to the recommended off state
* show an upload warning when it’s left on 
* add an auto fix to generate a layer with the default states to then FX layer and then disable all write defaults states
title: SDK guardrails are needed to protect against accidental or uninformed write defaults
